purpose: Resolve strict-G9 fee-classification assumptions for a single nonprofessional end user consuming realtime UTP Tape-C through an API/uncontrolled product.
primary_source_findings: UTP Data Policies expressly lists Application Program Interface (API) as an Uncontrolled Product.

The current UTP Detailed Usage Reporting Codes document, updated 2024-10 with fees as of 2025, defines UTP1APIS = Real-Time Nonprofessional Uncontrolled Recipient and assesses $1/month, billable to the Vendor.

That supplemental document states that a qualifying Nonprofessional Uncontrolled Product Recipient may be reported at Nonprofessional rates when separately identified by the Vendor, with no redistribution and use restricted to one Subscriber.
The same supplemental footnote expressly prohibits third-party software only for the Professional Uncontrolled Recipient exception; it does not repeat that sentence in the Nonprofessional footnote.

However, the older September-2023 general Data Policies text contains a broader final sentence saying higher rates may apply when an Uncontrolled Recipient uses third-party software. Therefore the interaction between the older general sentence and the newer specialized UTP1APIS code cannot be assumed away without provider/UTP classification evidence.

The fee is assessed to the Vendor under UTP1APIS. Therefore permanent-$0 to the end user is economically possible if a qualifying vendor lawfully classifies the user under the nonprofessional uncontrolled category and absorbs the $1 monthly assessment.

strict_g9_effect.old_overbroad_assumption_rejected: API AUTOMATION DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY IMPLY THE $3500 OWN-BEHALF NONDISPLAY FEE FOR A SINGLE QUALIFYING NONPROFESSIONAL RECIPIENT.
new_required_provider_proof: Provider identifies its realtime Tape-C/NBBO upstream lineage or licensed redistributor.
Provider confirms the exact single-user automated API entitlement is lawful under UTP1APIS or an equivalent approved nonprofessional uncontrolled classification.
Provider absorbs any upstream/vendor assessment so the end user remains permanently $0.
No balance, funding, activity, account-maintenance, subscription, per-query or other end-user monetary condition.
No redistribution; one subscriber; user qualification as nonprofessional must be actually established by the provider rather than assumed by XRAY.

paper_invest_implication: Paper Basic's $0/free-forever API + realtime NBBO + bot/algorithmic use is now economically compatible with strict G9-C in principle. C is not PROVEN until Paper identifies/attests its approved market-data classification and fee absorption (or equivalent licensed redistributor entitlement).
